name: lz4
one_liner: A tool that shrinks files and data streams extremely fast so they take up less space or less bandwidth to send.
buyer: A firmware engineer at an IoT or embedded-device company who needs to shrink sensor data before sending it over a slow, expensive radio or cellular link.
business_use_cases: A device maker compresses sensor logs with it before uploading over cheap LoRa or cellular connections, cutting their monthly data costs.
A game studio compresses asset bundles so players download updates faster, reducing server bandwidth bills.
A backend team compresses logs or CDN payloads to shrink their egress bill.

money_ideas.idea: A one-off consulting audit that retrofits LZ4 compression into a client's IoT or logging pipeline to cut their bandwidth or storage bill, billed as a project.

steal_this: Honestly, there isn't a new weekend business here — this is mature, widely-embedded infrastructure (it's already inside the Linux kernel and countless products), not a product on its own. The only real play is a one-off consulting gig: find a client paying too much for bandwidth or storage and drop LZ4 into their pipeline.
